references.text: Parallel text describing the actual making of the curtain with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim in skillfully woven work.
The same materials (blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen) and cherubim are used for the tabernacle's covering.
The list of materials to be gathered for the tabernacle, including blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
The curtain separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, where the atonement cover is. The high priest could enter behind the curtain only once a year.
The curtain is mentioned in connection with the Levites' duties when the camp was to be broken up.
Solomon's temple also had a curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen with cherubim on it.
The curtain is used as an image of the way into the sanctuary, which Jesus has opened for us.
The curtain that separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place in the tabernacle is explained in connection with Christ's perfect sacrifice.
The curtain symbolizes Jesus' body, and through his sacrifice we have boldness to enter the sanctuary.
When Jesus died, the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom, as a sign that the way to God is now open.
Mark also tells us that the temple curtain was torn in two when Jesus died.
Luke describes how the temple curtain was torn in half at Jesus' death.
